missionPremise: P-223 (SEV-1, 2026-09-15) was measured the same day and refuted for the tier-gate-bypass framing: the measuring account was Studio, so list_purchased_records returning ok/jobs:[] and read_purchased_record reaching the query were both consistent with a PASSING gate, not a bypassed one. Two things survived measurement and are this row's mandate: (1) a bad artifactId on read_purchased_record returns a raw, unhandled postgres-js error disclosing records_request_artifacts' table and column names verbatim to an authenticated caller; (2) the tier gate has never been observed REFUSING (a genuinely sub-Studio account could not be constructed by the earlier measurement), so 'the gate is dormant vs. correct' remains undistinguished per ENFORCEMENT's verify-by-violation rule. The coming-soon surface-change half of P-223 is explicitly NOT this row's mandate (unruled, held for a second dispatch).
falsifiersPreRegistered: 1. Prove the gate by violation: construct the sub-Studio case the earlier measurement could not, and show the refusal. If a real account cannot be created, build the test at the level where the entitlement is resolved and assert the refusal there, stating plainly that the live account path remains unexercised.
2. Delete the gate and confirm the test goes red. A test that passes with the control removed is testing nothing.
3. Enumerate every path that can produce a raw driver error, not just the one artifactId case reported.
4. Confirm no schema text survives anywhere in the refusal, including in a nested cause, a log line the caller can read back, or a stack. Grep the served payload for the table name.
5. If the tier gate genuinely does fire and the earlier row was pessimistic, the row still closes, with the evidence -- an honest refutation is a result.

designPlan.approach: (1) Add a UUID-format pre-check on artifactId in readPurchasedRecord, returning a NEW distinct reason artifact_id_malformed (never collapsed into artifact_not_found), mirroring this file's own existing invalidParcelNodeIdResult pattern for parcelNodeId -- house style, not a new shape. (2) Wrap every remaining DB call in both exported functions in a shared runQuery try/catch helper that logs the real error server-side (console.error, matching connection-record.ts's established '[smartsite-mcp] ...' logging convention) and returns a generic records_lookup_failed refusal on any OTHER unexpected driver failure, so no future call site can regress the same disclosure class even from a cause other than a malformed UUID. (3) For the tier gate: canRunStudioReport(snap) is a pure synchronous predicate over an already-resolved SmartsiteEntitlementSnapshot (requireAuthContext() reads AsyncLocalStorage populated once per request by the HTTP layer) -- so 'the level where entitlement is resolved', per falsifier 1's own fallback language, is exactly this snapshot object; no live account or DB is needed to exercise it. Add a PAID-Solo (subscriptionTier:'solo') refusal case alongside the pre-existing FREE case (found already merged 2026-09-03 in this file, predating this dispatch), since 'sub-Studio' is not only the free/null case and canRunStudioReport's real branch point is subscriptionTier, not the coarser tier field. Add a DB-less spy test using a fake db whose select() throws if called, proving the gate runs BEFORE any query is built (stronger than asserting response shape alone) -- and use that same spy harness to literally perform falsifier 2 (temporarily delete each gate check, confirm red, revert) before writing the close.
designPlan.existingCoverageFound_notReinvented: artifacts/smartsite-mcp/tests/records-extraction.test.ts already contains a FREE-tier refusal assertion for both tools, dated to the original P-113 commit (2026-09-03, c34ab0fc), 12 days before this dispatch. This is a real, non-trivial finding for the close per DEV_PROCESS 3.2/'an honest refutation is a result': the row's framing ('nobody has ever seen the gate refuse') is true at the LIVE production-account level (confirmed above) but was already partially false at the unit level before this lane started. This lane does not re-claim that prior work; it extends it (Solo case, spy-based non-vacuousness proof) and states the distinction plainly in the close.
designPlan.scopeDecision_artifactIdVsParcelNodeId: Per the dispatch's own 'Known trap': a malformed artifactId and a well-formed-but-nonexistent/not-owned one are declared as DIFFERENT reasons (artifact_id_malformed vs. the existing artifact_not_found), because a malformed id is the caller's own syntax error and carries no ownership-privacy concern, whereas the existing artifact_not_found envelope is deliberately silent about ownership mismatches (per this tool's own published description) and must not be diluted by conflating it with a client bug.
